The Genetics of the Interface: Towards a methodology for Innovation in Interaction Design

A fully funded international PhD at the intersection of Human Computer Interaction and Philosophy of Technology. Based at ENAC in Toulouse France, and with the opportunity to spend some of your time at Aalborg University’s Human Augmentation and Collaboration group.

❓What drives innovation and breakthroughs in interaction design? Mouse interactions and touchscreen gestures like pinches and swipes have become so successful that they now seem a natural part of our behaviour. Yet, designers create many new forms of interaction every year, and most fail to catch on. In this PhD project you will investigate the mechanisms behind how interaction techniques emerge, evolve, and ultimately succeed or fail, influenced by technical, human, and social factors.

👨‍🎓👩‍🎓 We have a great supervision team lined up. Your primary supervisors will be Catherine Letondal (ENAC, France) and Dan Bennett (Aalborg University, Denmark). You will also receive additional support from ACM Fellow Michel Beaudouin-Lafon (LISN, HCI), Stéphane Conversy (ENAC, HCI), and Guillaume Giroud (IRPHIL, Philosophy).

🗓 Deadline: 23rd November
